_scope_definitions.all: Every design the paper itself calls a regression-discontinuity (RD/RDD) design, i.e. it states that treatment is assigned by whether a running/forcing/assignment score crosses a fixed cutoff. Fires on the paper's own RD self-description; a paper that never claims an RD/threshold design is out of module.
_scope_definitions.covariate_adjusted: Fires only when the paper states it adds covariates to the RD estimating specification or otherwise conditions its point estimate on covariates. Near-miss that does NOT fire: reporting covariate balance purely as a diagnostic while the headline estimate is unadjusted.
_scope_definitions.fuzzy_rd: Fires only when the paper states its design is fuzzy / has imperfect compliance at the cutoff (the probability of treatment jumps by less than one, or it instruments received treatment with the cutoff indicator). Near-miss that does NOT fire: a sharp design the paper describes as perfect/deterministic compliance; using an instrumental variable elsewhere in the paper unrelated to the cutoff.
_scope_definitions.fuzzy: Fires only when the paper itself describes its design as fuzzy: it states that treatment take-up changes probabilistically (not deterministically) at the cutoff, or that it uses the cutoff/assignment indicator as an instrument for treatment actually received. NOT fired by: a sharp design that mentions occasional non-compliance in passing, or a paper that merely reports imperfect data coverage. If the paper never declares probabilistic take-up or an instrumenting step, the design is out of scope (NA).
_scope_definitions.pcrd: Fires only when the paper defines its RD treatment as a predetermined characteristic of the winning unit/candidate (a politician-characteristic RD), so the contrast is winners of differing types. Near-miss that does NOT fire: a standard party- or incumbency-status close-election RD where treatment is which party/incumbent won, not a candidate trait.
_scope_definitions.local_poly_datadriven: Fires only when the paper states it estimates the RD effect with local polynomial (local linear/quadratic) regression using a data-driven bandwidth it names (MSE-optimal, CER-optimal, cross-validated, or a plug-in selector). Near-miss that does NOT fire: a global polynomial fit over the full range with no bandwidth; a single ad hoc window the paper picks without naming a data-driven selector.
_scope_definitions.clustered: Fires only when the paper states its observation structure is grouped or repeated (multiple observations per unit, a panel of repeated events, or an explicit clustering/grouping level). Keys on the declared data structure, not on whether cluster-robust errors were used. NOT fired by: a single cross-section with one observation per unit. Ambiguous cases are NA.
_scope_definitions.discrete_rv: Fires only when the paper states its running variable is discrete or has few mass points (integer counts, coarse bins). Near-miss that does NOT fire: a continuous running variable rounded only for display; a continuous variable with many distinct values.
_scope_definitions.geographic_rd: Fires only when the paper states it uses a geographic/boundary RD with a spatial (two-dimensional) score or distance-to-a-border running variable. Near-miss that does NOT fire: a one-dimensional non-spatial score; a design that merely includes region fixed effects.
_scope_definitions.multiple_tests: Fires only when the paper reports a battery of several covariate-balance, placebo, or multiple-outcome tests (its own stated set of two or more such tests). Near-miss that does NOT fire: a single balance test or a single outcome.
_scope_definitions.heaped_rv: Fires only when the paper states its running variable heaps/bunches at particular (e.g. round) values. Near-miss that does NOT fire: a smooth continuous density with no reported heaping.

claim: Because the fitted shape of the running variable drives the estimate, the paper must show the result holds under more than one functional form / polynomial order.
observable: Whether the paper reports its RD estimate under two or more functional-form specifications (e.g. two polynomial orders or a local-vs-parametric comparison).
pass_condition: The paper reports the estimate under two or more distinct functional-form or polynomial-order specifications.
flag_condition: The paper reports the estimate under a single functional form with no specification-variation check.
severity_basis: Hall (2015) and Gelman (2017): estimates are sensitive to functional form / polynomial order and must be shown insensitive.
requirement_statement: The paper must report its RD estimate under two or more functional-form specifications.

claim: A break in the running variable's density at the cutoff is a signature of sorting, so the paper must run a test for such a break.
observable: Whether the paper reports a test (or diagnostic) of the running-variable density for a discontinuity at the cutoff.
pass_condition: The paper reports a running-variable density / manipulation test (e.g. a McCrary-type test or an equivalent density-continuity diagnostic) at the cutoff.
flag_condition: The paper never examines the running-variable density for a discontinuity at the cutoff.
severity_basis: Lemieux (2007) and Trounstine (2011): a continuous running-variable density is required for the design to be valid.
requirement_statement: The paper must test the running-variable density for a discontinuity at the cutoff.

claim: A valid design implies predetermined characteristics are balanced at the cutoff, so the paper must test predetermined covariates for a discontinuity there.
observable: Whether the paper reports balance / continuity tests on predetermined covariates at the cutoff (e.g. re-running the RD with covariates as outcomes).
pass_condition: The paper reports covariate balance / continuity checks on predetermined characteristics at the cutoff.
flag_condition: The paper reports no covariate balance or continuity check at the cutoff.
severity_basis: Caughey (2011a): the testable implication of continuity is that pretreatment characteristics do not differ at the cutoff.
requirement_statement: The paper must test predetermined covariates for balance / continuity at the cutoff.

claim: Because a jump should appear only at the true cutoff, estimating at placebo cutoffs is a falsification aid; the paper should report such placebo-cutoff estimates, though this evidence is supportive rather than decisive for continuity at the cutoff.
observable: Whether the paper reports RD estimates at artificial / placebo cutoff values away from the true cutoff.
pass_condition: The paper reports estimates at one or more placebo cutoff values (or placebo points where no effect should appear).
flag_condition: The paper reports no placebo-cutoff / placebo-point check.
severity_basis: Cattaneo (2019b): the design implies no significant effect at placebo cutoff values, and discontinuities away from the cutoff cast doubt on it -- though the source notes such evidence is neither necessary nor sufficient, so absence is a soft (MEDIUM) flag.
requirement_statement: The paper should report a placebo-cutoff falsification check (RD estimates at cutoff values where no effect is expected).

claim: Running many balance, placebo, or outcome tests will turn up chance rejections, so a paper reporting a battery of such tests must correct for multiple comparisons.
observable: For a paper reporting several covariate-balance, placebo, or multiple-outcome tests, whether it applies a multiple-comparisons correction (or a joint test) before reading individual rejections.
pass_condition: The paper applies a multiple-testing correction or reports a joint test when interpreting its battery of tests.
flag_condition: The paper reports many separate tests and reads individual significant results at face value without any multiplicity adjustment.
severity_basis: Eggers (2014) and Cuesta (2016): enough tests will yield chance rejections even when the design holds.
requirement_statement: When interpreting a battery of balance/placebo/outcome tests, the paper should apply a multiple-comparisons correction or report a joint/omnibus test rather than reading individual rejections at face value.

evidence.quote: If we test for differences between winners and losers in a large enough set of variables, we will eventually find it by chance even if the assumptions underlying RD are in fact met.
the more statistical tests one conducts, the more likely one is to discover false positives even when all the null hypotheses are true.

author_guidance: State explicitly that the RD estimate is a local effect at the cutoff (for compliers, in a fuzzy design) and does not by itself identify a population-wide average effect; if you generalize beyond the cutoff, name the extra assumption you rely on.
claim: The RD estimand is a local effect at the cutoff, so the paper should characterize it as such rather than as a population-wide average effect.
observable: Whether the paper states that its estimate is local to the cutoff (and, if fuzzy, applies to compliers) rather than presenting it as a general population effect.
pass_condition: The paper describes its estimand as local to the cutoff, or names the additional assumption it invokes to generalize.
flag_condition: The paper presents its RD estimate as a population-wide/average effect without noting its locality or any extrapolation assumption.
severity_basis: Boas (2011) and Gerber (2011): the RD estimand is a local effect at the threshold, not the overall population effect.
requirement_statement: The paper should interpret its RD estimate as local to the cutoff, not as a population-wide effect.

claim: When the running variable heaps and the heaping is related to outcomes, standard RD diagnostics miss the resulting bias, so a paper with a heaped running variable must run supplementary heaping checks.
observable: For a paper whose running variable heaps, whether it reports checks aimed at heaping-induced composition bias (e.g. disaggregated heaped-vs-non-heaped plots, a donut estimate dropping heap points, or covariate tests at heaps).
pass_condition: The paper reports a heaping-specific diagnostic or remedy beyond the standard density/balance checks.
flag_condition: The paper's running variable heaps but it reports only standard diagnostics and no heaping-specific check.
severity_basis: Barreca (2011): standard diagnostics miss heaping-induced composition bias, so supplementary checks are needed.
requirement_statement: A paper with a heaped running variable must run supplementary heaping-specific checks.

evidence.quote: regression-discontinuity designs arrive at biased estimates when attributes related to outcomes predict heaping in the running variable
